children: Niagen Bioscience said an independent Nature Communications preclinical study identified CD38 as a driver of age-related NAD+ decline and found NR restored NAD+ and improved pregnancy outcomes in aged mice. The NR used was not the company’s Niagen product.
CD38 drives NAD+ decline with age
Supports the company’s NAD+ thesis; could boost interest in NAD+ modulators.
NR improved outcomes in aged mice
Signals potential therapeutic relevance; may lift demand for NR pending human data.
Older placentas had lower NAD+ levels
Human tissue link adds translational weight; supports market narrative.
NR not consumed by CD38; NMN is
Positions NR more favorably vs NMN in high-CD38 tissues.
Study independent; not funded by NAGE
Reduces bias concerns but limits control; still reputational upside.

This is early-stage, third-party preclinical validation aligning with Niagen’s NAD+ platform narrative. A clear catalyst would be human clinical data showing NR improves pregnancy-related endpoints or regulatory steps advancing NR-based therapies.
